string.text: Ammo Container
Old Ammo Box
An old, noisy steel ammunition box from abandoned army surplus. It is locked with a simple lock.\n \n

A water-resistant container used to store ammunition or weapon magazines. It is common among hunters and wealthy stalkers, and is a good find in the Zone. Such containers usually come with a large supply of factory-made ammunition, and their water-resistant construction keeps the rounds from getting damp. Most ammunition in the Zone is old, damaged, or hand-loaded by stalkers with poor-quality equipment. Good rounds are therefore highly valued and quite rare.\n \n
Coin Slot Case
A sealed, heavy case with a strange symbol and a coin slot too large for ordinary rubles. What opens it?\n \n

A waterproof, electromagnetic-radiation-resistant container. Ecologists mainly use it to transport scientific instruments and research samples. After several incidents in which equipment failed due to anomalous fields, the Ministry of Science authorized specialized containers for carrying equipment in the field. Mercenaries may also use them to store equipment and additional protective gear. The container also has a special sterile compartment for field samples.\n \n
Ecologist Field Container
Metal Food Container
A radiation-shielded metal container for perishable food. Rare in the Zone and prized for keeping drinks cold.\n \n
Scavenger’s Box
A large box of assorted belongings, locked with a simple lock. Perhaps someone’s stash of junk.\n \n
Medical Case
A sterile locked case with compartments for first-aid supplies, usually carried by medics.\n \n
Sniper Rifle Case
A rugged, waterproof case for sniper rifles of any length.\n \n
Locked Tackle Box
A fishing tackle box repurposed for storage. Since there are no fish in the Zone, it may hold something more useful than bait.\n \n
Tool Kit
A latched tool case used by technicians. It only fits tools and spare parts, perhaps an old pack of cigarettes. Good tools are valuable, so it is locked.\n \n
Strange Tokens
Large silver coins stamped with a strange symbol. They have no monetary value, but invite curiosity; the markings resemble Cyrillic or perhaps Japanese.\n \n
